identity.title: RefineStat: Efficient Exploration for Probabilistic Program Synthesis

problem.claim: Statistical model discovery and probabilistic-program generation require navigating a large, domain-constrained search space while avoiding syntactic and semantic errors.

gap.claim: Small language models frequently generate probabilistic programs with syntactic or semantic flaws, including invalid inference constructs.

contributions.claim: Introduces RefineStat, a language-model-driven framework that enforces semantic constraints and diagnostically refines programs by resampling prior or likelihood components when reliability checks fail.
Reports evaluation of RefineStat on multiple probabilistic-programming code-generation tasks using smaller language models.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors distinguish RefineStat by combining semantic validity constraints with diagnostic-aware component resampling, motivated by probabilistic programmers’ expertise and debugging strategies.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that RefineStat produces syntactically sound and statistically reliable programs on the evaluated tasks.
The authors report that RefineStat often matches or surpasses outputs from closed-source large language models, including OpenAI o3.

narrative_sequence.summary: Probabilistic-program statistical model discovery involves a large search space and strict domain-specific constraints.
Small language models frequently produce probabilistic programs with syntactic and semantic errors, including flawed inference constructs.
RefineStat enforces valid distributions and well-formed parameters, then uses reliability diagnostics to resample prior or likelihood components.
Across multiple code-generation tasks with smaller language models, the authors report syntactic soundness, statistical reliability, and frequent parity or advantage over closed-source large models.

source_observation.claim: The framework pairs explicit semantic constraints with failure-triggered, component-level refinement rather than relying only on initial generation.

lessons.interpretation: Separating validity checks from targeted repair can align a method’s intervention with the specific failure signal.
lessons.application: For a constrained generation task, define checkable invariants and resample or revise only the component implicated by a failed diagnostic.
lessons.exception: This move is unsuitable when failures cannot be localized reliably or when component changes have strongly coupled effects.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the evaluated tasks, datasets, model configurations, reliability metrics, or statistical test conditions.
The frequency and magnitude of cases where RefineStat matches or surpasses OpenAI o3 are unspecified.
